# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- Prefer the smallest exact span that is one complete answer value, not the shortest notation or a bundle of equivalent notations.
- Before copying, treat every substantive qualifier in the question as a selector, including a specific row, column, or field label, an ordinal or period such as a particular quarter, a parent entity or product name, a requested branch or variant, and a region. Locate the single candidate whose surrounding header, label, or section supports all such qualifiers simultaneously, then read the value at that exact intersection. Do not substitute an adjacent total, another column or row, another product type, or another nearby item merely because it shares the numeric format or general category. For a table, verify that the chosen cell aligns with both the requested row qualifier and the requested column or header qualifier; for a named parent entity or product with a requested branch or variant, locate the section headed by that parent and return the labeled variant that answers the request.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly from the document whenever possible.
- For date questions (for example, "What date..." or "On which date..."), select the printed date value belonging to the relevant field or label. If that selected value is only a month and day, return that printed month-day span and do not append a year from another part of the document. Keep a year that is visibly part of the selected printed date; if the question explicitly asks for a year or a year-bearing period, include the year as requested. Apply the same principle to other date granularities: preserve an explicitly requested component and do not merge components from separate fields into a more complete-looking date. This is assessed from the document; do not strip a year that is visibly part of the relevant date field.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase.
- When a value appears in more than one form (for example, figures or currency notation plus a spelled-out amount), return only the single form selected by the question's field or nearby label; do not append the alternate form in parentheses or as a second notation. If the question explicitly requests both forms, provide both in the requested form; otherwise, use one exact span.
- Keep the components required to identify the value when they are visibly attached to the selected printed value, including units, qualifiers, and a parenthetical acronym that is part of a printed name; for entity-name answers, generic category descriptors and non-distinguishing location or branch extensions are not required identifying components; do not add a parenthetical restatement or definition. Copy the selected span's spelling and punctuation literally, except that quotation marks are rendered as specified below. For any quoted span in the selected answer, including a title, term, label, or parenthetical acronym, render its quotation marks as plain ASCII straight quotation marks (straight double quotes for a double-quoted span), not curly or typographic quotes, and do not insert an extra space before a parenthesis. Preserve the selected span's words, capitalization, spelling, internal punctuation, parenthetical content, and spacing. Replace only the typographic quotation-mark characters with their plain ASCII equivalents; do not otherwise add or remove quotation marks around the selected value. This rule changes only the quotation-mark characters and does not normalize other punctuation: keep exact-copy handling for separators and symbols, and do not strip or insert a slash or other separator in a numeric identifier unless that follows from the visible selected value.
- When the question asks to identify or name an entity (a company, brand, service, organization, or person), return the distinctive proper-name portion that identifies it. If the printed span combines that name with generic category words that restate the category already named in the question (for example, words equivalent to "rent-a-car system", "company", "service", or "corporation"), do not append those generic descriptive words, even when they are printed adjacent as part of one line or trade-name phrase. If the same printed phrase includes a location or branch extension that is not needed to distinguish this entity from another plausible candidate on the page and is not requested by the question, omit that extension as well; do not strip a word when doing so would split an integral proper name into a different or incomplete name.
- For entity-name answers, retain honorifics and personal titles that precede a printed name, printed units and currency symbols attached to the selected value, a parenthetical acronym that is part of the printed name, and any word that actually distinguishes this entity from another plausible candidate on the page (for example, a geographic or branch qualifier that separates two otherwise identical names, or a word the question itself asks for). Drop words that merely restate the question's category and add no distinguishing information; do not append a location or branch extension solely because it is printed next to the name.
- Exceptions: if the question explicitly asks for the full, formal, legal, or printed-in-full name or otherwise requests the complete phrase, return that full span. If the question asks what kind or type of document, item, or slip something is, return the complete printed type label. This rule applies only to the name of an identified entity, not to document-type labels, titles of meetings, or topics.
- Do not answer with an explanation, a list of candidate names, or a hedge; return a single exact span inside <answer>...</answer>. Judge from the visible layout whether a printed phrase is a single trade name with a category descriptor and whether a location or branch extension is needed for identification.
- Resolve unit and symbol handling from the selected printed value, not from the question wording or a nearby column heading. When the selected cell or entry prints only a number and the percent sign or other unit appears only in the question or in a heading shared by the column, return the printed number alone; for a "What %" question, this can mean returning 39 rather than 39%. Preserve a unit or symbol when it is visibly attached to the selected printed value, such as a printed monetary amount like $268,007.47. Do not append a parenthetical restatement or an alternate notation.
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and confirm that the single retained, best-supported exact span satisfies every substantive qualifier identified above.
